a2149447.text:
Feature: declare the invitation routes' permission, and lint the error helpers in CI.

Route permissions are declared with require(Perm.X) in a route's dependencies and read back from app.routes by the route-permission test (tests/integration_tests/test_route_permissions.py). The two invitation routes still check the caller's can_invite flag by hand inside the handler, so they are missing from that registry, and controllers all over the tree still raise HTTPException(403) / HTTPException(404) directly with hand-built ErrorResponse bodies.

Expected:
- POST /api/households/invitations and POST /api/households/invitations/email declare Perm.GROUP_INVITE through require(); the hand-written can_invite checks go. A user without can_invite answers 403 before the body is read or validated (an empty body still answers 403); a user with it is not refused.
- The declared-permission table therefore gains a GROUP_INVITE entry with exactly those two routes. Nothing else changes permission: GROUP_ORGANIZE keeps POST/PUT merge/PUT item/DELETE item on /api/foods, POST merge on /api/groups/labels, POST/POST merge/PUT item/DELETE item on /api/organizers/categories and /api/organizers/tags, POST merge on /api/organizers/tools; GROUP_MANAGE keeps the /api/groups/ai-providers routes (providers create, test, get/put/delete/test by id, prompts get/put/delete, settings get/put), PUT /api/groups/preferences, GET /api/households/members and PUT /api/households/permissions; HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE keeps POST/DELETE /api/households/mealplans/ical and PUT /api/households/preferences.
- The helpers in mealie.routes._base.permissions become forbidden(message=None) and not_found(message=None): the HTTPException carries an ErrorResponse detail with the message only when one is given (the frontend shows detail.message as a toast), a bare status otherwise. Every route or route helper that answers 403 or 404 builds the exception with them, keeping its current message where it had one (for example "Permission Denied", "Comment does not belong to user", "User cannot edit other users", "User Registration is Disabled", "Token Not Found", the translated meal-plan "no recipes match your rules" message). Status codes do not change anywhere.
- A semgrep rule under .semgrep/ flags HTTPException raised directly with a 403 or 404 status in route code, with a Taskfile task to run it and a step in the backend CI workflow.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/test_route_permissions.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
a2149447.notes: The rejection test sends an empty body, so the 403 must come before validation (stated); the declared-permission table is the other target; the helper signatures and the semgrep rule are stated as the feature but not graded. The full table had to be restated so the agent does not add or drop any other route.

f2873227.text:
Fix: bulk update and bulk delete in the generic repository ignore the repository's group/household scope.

RepositoryGeneric.update_many and delete_many select rows by id only, while every other read and write of a group- or household-scoped repository applies the scope filter. Through the shopping list item routes this lets a member of one household change or remove items of another household's shopping list in the same group: PUT /api/households/shopping/items/{item_id} and the bulk PUT /api/households/shopping/items update them, DELETE /api/households/shopping/items/{item_id} and the bulk DELETE /api/households/shopping/items?ids=... remove them.

Expected:
- update_many and delete_many apply the same group/household filter as the repository's other queries: rows outside the caller's scope are neither updated nor deleted, and are not returned.
- A user of household A sending an update for an item of a list owned by a user of household B (single-item route or bulk route, with the item's id in the body) gets 200 with an empty updatedItems list, and the item is unchanged when its owner reads it back.
- The same user deleting such an item (single-item route, or the bulk route with the id in ids) gets 200 and the item still exists for its owner.
- Items within the caller's scope behave exactly as today.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests tests/integration_tests/public_explorer_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
f2873227.notes: The tests assert 200 with no effect rather than 403/404, which is stated as is. The commit also corrects the public recipes test so household-2 recipes are created as the household-2 user; nothing to state for the agent.

eddb0c30.text:
Fix: recipe assets can be uploaded with scriptable extensions and are served inline.

POST /api/recipes/{slug}/assets stores whatever extension the client declares, and GET /api/media/recipes/{recipe_id}/assets/{file_name} serves the file inline. An html, svg or js asset is therefore rendered by the browser from the application's origin: stored XSS for anyone who can view the recipe.

Expected:
- The asset upload accepts only these extensions, compared case-insensitively: pdf, jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, bmp, avif, txt, md, csv, json. Any other declared extension (html, htm, xhtml, svg, js, ...) answers 400 with the detail "Unsupported file extension", and nothing is stored.
- Allowed uploads work as before: 200 with the asset record.
- The asset download route sends the file as an attachment: a Content-Disposition: attachment header carrying the file's name, so a browser downloads it instead of rendering it.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
eddb0c30.notes: The Content-Disposition change is part of the fix but no test checks it.

c935e04f.text:
Feature: declare route permissions with a require() dependency.

Each handler that needs a user permission calls self.checks.can_manage(), self.checks.can_organize() and so on (the OperationChecks helper on BaseUserController) somewhere in its body. Nothing can list which route needs which permission, so a forgotten check is invisible in review.

Expected:
- A new module mealie.routes._base.permissions with:
  - Perm, a StrEnum: ANY_VALID_USER = "any_valid_user", GROUP_ORGANIZE = "group:organize", GROUP_MANAGE = "group:manage", GROUP_INVITE = "group:invite", HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE = "household:manage". The flags: GROUP_ORGANIZE needs can_organize, GROUP_MANAGE can_manage, GROUP_INVITE can_invite, HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE can_manage_household; ANY_VALID_USER accepts every signed-in user.
  - RequirePermission(perm): a callable dependency that keeps the permission as .perm, takes the current user (get_current_user) and raises HTTPException 403 when the user lacks the flag. Calling it directly with a PrivateUser works (PrivateUser.model_construct(can_manage=True) passes, can_manage=False raises with status_code 403; RequirePermission(Perm.ANY_VALID_USER)(PrivateUser.model_construct()) passes).
  - require(perm) returns Depends(RequirePermission(perm)), for a route's dependencies list, so the instance stays on the route's dependant and the declared permission can be read back from app.routes (iterate the route contexts, look at each APIRoute's dependant.dependencies for a RequirePermission call).
  - forbidden() -> HTTPException 403; not_found(message="Not found.") -> HTTPException 404 with an ErrorResponse detail. HttpRepo's 404s use not_found().
- The routes declare exactly this table (method, path), and no other route declares a permission:
  - GROUP_ORGANIZE: POST /api/foods, PUT /api/foods/merge, PUT /api/foods/{item_id}, DELETE /api/foods/{item_id}, POST /api/groups/labels/merge, POST /api/organizers/categories, POST /api/organizers/categories/merge, PUT /api/organizers/categories/{item_id}, DELETE /api/organizers/categories/{item_id}, POST /api/organizers/tags, POST /api/organizers/tags/merge, PUT /api/organizers/tags/{item_id}, DELETE /api/organizers/tags/{item_id}, POST /api/organizers/tools/merge.
  - GROUP_MANAGE: POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers, POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/test, GET, PUT and DELETE /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/{provider_id}, POST /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/{provider_id}/test, GET /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts, PUT and DELETE /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts/{prompt_name}, GET and PUT /api/groups/ai-providers/settings, PUT /api/groups/preferences, GET /api/households/members, PUT /api/households/permissions.
  - HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE: POST and DELETE /api/households/mealplans/ical, PUT /api/households/preferences.
- The in-handler checks, OperationChecks and the checks property are removed; who gets 403 does not change.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/test_route_permissions.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
c935e04f.notes: The test introspects app.routes for RequirePermission instances and calls the dependency directly, so the class name, the .perm attribute, the enum values and the whole route table are load-bearing and had to be spelled out.

250d4996.text:
Fix: the household member list and the group preferences are open to every member.

GET /api/households/members returns every user of the caller's household, with e-mail addresses and permission flags, to any signed-in member, and PUT /api/groups/preferences lets any member change the group's preferences. Both are management functions and should be behind the caller's can_manage flag, like PUT /api/households/permissions already is.

Expected:
- GET /api/households/members answers 403 for a user whose can_manage is false. For a user with can_manage it answers 200 with the paginated list as today, still limited to the caller's household (perPage=-1 returns them all; a user of another household is not listed).
- PUT /api/groups/preferences answers 403 without can_manage and updates the preferences as today with it.
- GET /api/groups/members, GET /api/groups/preferences and the household's own preferences routes are unchanged.
- Frontend: the profile page shows the "total users" statistics card only to users who can manage (not graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
250d4996.notes: The existing members test now grants can_manage to its caller first; the group preferences check is in the fix but has no test.

e3cf55b9.text:
Feature: recipe counts on tags and categories, and a merge action for each.

The group data pages for tags and categories cannot show how many recipes use each organizer, and duplicates ("Dessert"/"Desserts") can only be cleaned up by editing every recipe.

Expected:
- Every tag returned by GET /api/organizers/tags and every category returned by GET /api/organizers/categories carries recipeCount: the number of recipes carrying it, 0 for an unused one. The single-item and merge responses carry it too.
- POST /api/organizers/tags/merge and POST /api/organizers/categories/merge, body {"fromId": <uuid>, "toId": <uuid>}, both behind the organize-group-data permission (403 without can_organize, like create/update/delete):
  - fromId equal to toId answers 400.
  - An unknown fromId or toId (not in the caller's group) answers 404.
  - Otherwise every recipe linked to the source is linked to the target instead; a recipe that already had both keeps a single link to the target (no unique-constraint error); the source is deleted. The response is 200 with the target (TagOut / CategoryOut, including recipeCount, which now counts the merged recipes: two sources with one recipe each give 2, one recipe with both gives 1). Afterwards GET of the source's id answers 404 and each affected recipe lists the target and not the source in tags / recipeCategory.
- Frontend (not graded): the tags and categories data pages show the count, offer "Merge" (pick the target) and "Delete unused".

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/category_tag_tool_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
e3cf55b9.notes: All tests of the new file are targets (recipe_count on lists, merge moves/overlap/404/400 for tags and categories).

742b498c.text:
Fix: deleting a recipe must require ownership, not merely edit rights.

Recipe deletion reuses the collaborative-editing rule: whoever may edit a recipe may delete it. Recipes are unlocked by default, so any member of the owner's household, and any member of another household when the owner's household allows edits from other households, can delete another user's recipes, one at a time through DELETE /api/recipes/{slug} and in bulk through POST /api/recipes/bulk-actions/delete. Editing a shared recipe is a feature; deleting it is not.

Expected:
- A recipe can be deleted only by its owner or by an administrator. The recipe's locked setting and the household preference "lock recipe edits from other households" play no part in deletion any more: a non-owner is refused even when the recipe is unlocked, and even when the owner's household allows edits from other households.
- DELETE /api/recipes/{slug} by a non-owner answers 403 and leaves the recipe in place (that user's GET of the recipe still answers 200 with the same id).
- POST /api/recipes/bulk-actions/delete answers 403 when any of the listed recipes is not owned by the caller, and deletes nothing in that case.
- The owner can still delete their recipe, and an admin can still delete any recipe in the group, including a locked recipe owned by someone else.
- Updating is unchanged: a non-owner may still edit an unlocked recipe under the existing household rules.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
742b498c.notes: The cross-household test is parametrized over the lock preference and the private flag; the request states the rule once for all four cases.

4b32e54b.text:
Fix: a refusal by a declared route permission carries no message, so the user sees nothing.

Routes that declare a permission with require(Perm.X) answer a bare 403 when the caller lacks the flag. The frontend only shows an error toast when the response body carries detail.message, so a user who clicks, say, "create tag" without the organize permission sees the action silently do nothing.

Expected:
- The permission dependency (RequirePermission.__call__) takes the request's translator as a second dependency (get_locale_provider) and refuses with forbidden(translator.t("exceptions.permission-denied")), so the 403 body is an ErrorResponse whose detail.message is the translated "exceptions.permission-denied" text ("You do not have permission to perform this action" in en-US, the other languages' files already have the key).
- Every route that declares a permission answers 403 with that message for a user without it; callers with the permission are unaffected.
- Calling the dependency directly now takes (user, translator): RequirePermission(perm)(user, get_locale_provider()) passes for a user with the flag and raises HTTPException 403 without it; RequirePermission(Perm.ANY_VALID_USER)(user, translator) always passes.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/test_route_permissions.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
4b32e54b.notes: test_route_rejects_user_without_permission is parametrized over every declared route; the request states the message once for all of them. The direct-call signature is load-bearing for the two unit-style tests.

f4b4f87e.text:
Fix: the organize permission must also cover units, tools, labels, recipe actions and the seeders.

The "User can organize group data" flag (can_organize) gates foods, tags and categories, declared on their routes with require(Perm.GROUP_ORGANIZE). Units, tools, multi-purpose labels, household recipe actions and the food/unit seeders are still open to every member, although the documentation describes the permission as covering organizers in general.

Expected:
- These routes declare Perm.GROUP_ORGANIZE through the route-permission dependency, so a user without can_organize gets 403 before the body is read or validated, and a user with it is not refused (any status other than 403, since the check runs first): POST /api/units, PUT /api/units/merge, PUT /api/units/{item_id}, DELETE /api/units/{item_id}; POST /api/organizers/tools, PUT /api/organizers/tools/{item_id}, DELETE /api/organizers/tools/{item_id}; POST /api/groups/labels, PUT /api/groups/labels/{item_id}, DELETE /api/groups/labels/{item_id}; POST /api/households/recipe-actions, PUT /api/households/recipe-actions/{item_id}, DELETE /api/households/recipe-actions/{item_id}; POST /api/groups/seeders/foods, POST /api/groups/seeders/units.
- The table of declared permissions read back from app.routes grows by exactly these entries under GROUP_ORGANIZE; no other route changes its declared permission.
- Reads (the lists, single items, /empty) stay open to every member.
- Docs: the permissions page and the frontend wording for the permission say it covers foods, units, tools, labels, tags, categories and recipe actions; a frontend announcement about the change is welcome (none of this is graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/test_route_permissions.py tests/integration_tests/category_tag_tool_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
f4b4f87e.notes: The merge test files change how they create another group's tool/label (through the repository, because that group's plain user loses the permission); that is test plumbing, not stated.

72c62e8c.text:
Fix: recipes imported from a zip ignore the household's "recipes are public by default" preference.

A recipe created through the API gets settings.public from the household preference recipePublic. A recipe imported from a Mealie export zip (POST /api/recipes/create/zip) keeps whatever public value the archive carries, so a household whose recipes are public by default ends up with private recipes it did not ask for (and the other way round).

Expected:
- POST /api/recipes/create/zip creates the recipe with settings.public equal to the importing user's household preference recipe_public, whatever the archive says: an export of a private recipe imported into a household with recipePublic true comes back with settings.public true; with recipePublic false it comes back private. When the archive has no settings block, a settings block is created with that value and the other defaults.
- Everything else still comes from the archive: re-importing an export preserves the recipe's contents, and its settings are identical to the original's except for public.
- The import still answers 201 with the new recipe's slug, which differs from the original's.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
72c62e8c.notes: The existing re-import test now compares settings with public excluded; stated as "identical except for public".

823b938a.text:
Fix: the "organize group data" permission is not enforced on foods, tags and categories.

Every user has a can_organize flag ("User can organize group data") and the controllers already have a can_organize check alongside can_manage, can_invite and can_manage_household, but the tag, category and food routes never call it: any member can create, rename, delete and merge them.

Expected:
- For a user without can_organize: POST /api/organizers/tags, POST /api/organizers/categories and POST /api/foods answer 403; PUT and DELETE on /api/organizers/tags/{item_id}, /api/organizers/categories/{item_id} and /api/foods/{item_id} answer 403; PUT /api/foods/merge answers 403. A refused call changes nothing.
- For a user with can_organize the same calls behave as today: create answers 201, update (PUT with the item's id and a new name) 200, delete 200, merge 200.
- Reads need no permission: GET on the three collections and GET of a single item answer 200 whatever the flag.
- The flag is read from the user at request time: granting or removing it takes effect on the next request.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
823b938a.notes: All tests of the new file are targets (create/update/delete for foods, tags, categories; food merge; reads stay open).

aa4473ec.text:
Fix: an admin cannot delete a group that still has households or recipes.

DELETE /api/admin/groups/{item_id} rightly refuses a group that still has users (400, "Cannot delete group with users"). But once the group's users are gone the delete still fails, because the group's households and recipes are not removed with it and the foreign keys block the row's deletion, so a group can never be removed once it has been used.

Expected:
- Deleting a group cascades to its households and its recipes (and what hangs off them), the way the group's other child rows already go with it.
- After deleting the group's users (DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} answers 200 for each), DELETE /api/admin/groups/{id} of a group that owned recipes answers 200, and GET /api/admin/groups/{id} afterwards answers 404.
- Deleting a group that has no households or recipes keeps working, and a group with users is still refused.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/admin_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

642c826f.text:
Fix: the query filter API can filter and sort on sensitive columns.

The queryFilter and orderBy parameters of the paginated endpoints resolve any column of the model, and through relationships any column of a related model. A member can therefore filter recipes on user.password or user.email (or tokens on their models) and extract the value character by character with LIKE. Only columns meant for filtering should be reachable.

Expected:
- A column must be marked to be usable in a query filter or an order_by. Introduce FilterableColumn[T] (module mealie.db.models._filterable_column, re-exported from mealie.db.models._model_base): a drop-in for Mapped[T] on scalar columns that sets the column's info {"filterable": True}. The base created_at and update_at columns are marked.
- QueryFilterBuilder.get_model_and_model_attr_from_attr_string raises NonFilterableValueError (a ValueError, message "Cannot filter on <column>", defined in mealie.services.query_filter.builder) when the resolved column is not marked: password and email on the User model, token on LongLiveToken, user.email and user.password reached from RecipeModel. A marked column resolves as before and returns the model and the attribute (full_name on User gives User and User.full_name; user.full_name from RecipeModel too); a single-hop association proxy that resolves to a marked column works (household_id on RecipeModel gives User and User.household_id). filter_query on a non-filterable attribute raises the same error.
- Mark every column the API filters or sorts today across the models (recipes and their settings, ingredients, nutrition, assets, extras, notes, timeline, shared tokens, tags, categories, tools, labels, units, foods, cookbooks, mealplans, shopping lists and items, households, groups and their preferences, users). On User only id, full_name, username, group_id and household_id are filterable; email, password, auth_method, admin, advanced, cache_key and the token columns are not.
- An order_by on a non-filterable column answers 400 with detail 'Invalid order_by statement "<order_by>": Cannot filter on <column>'; a query filter on one answers 400 like any invalid filter.
- The labels model moves next to the other recipe models: MultiPurposeLabel is imported from mealie.db.models.recipe.labels (the migration dded3119c1fe, the migration data fix and the model registry follow; mealie.db.models.labels no longer exists).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/repository_tests tests/unit_tests/services_tests/backup_v2_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
642c826f.notes: The exact set of columns marked filterable is long; the request gives the rule, the models and the User exceptions the tests check. The backup tests, and the two pre-existing as-json tests of the builder, are targets only because their modules import the moved labels module / the new error class; both module paths are stated.

643c4901.text:
Fix: admins cannot edit recipes owned by users of other households.

The recipe update permission check treats an admin like any other non-owner. When a recipe's owner belongs to another household and that household keeps "lock recipe edits from other households" on (the default), an admin's PUT /api/recipes/{slug} is refused with 403. Admins can already delete any recipe in the group; they should be able to edit any recipe too.

Expected:
- For an administrator the update check always passes: PUT /api/recipes/{slug} (and everything behind the same check: PATCH, image upload and image delete) on a recipe owned by a user of another household answers 200 whatever that household's private_household and lock_recipe_edits_from_other_households preferences are, and a following GET /api/recipes/{slug} returns the updated name.
- Non-admin rules are unchanged: the owner can always edit; a non-owner cannot edit a locked recipe; a non-owner from another household is refused when the owner's household locks edits from other households.
- Frontend: useRecipePermissions reports canEditRecipe true for an admin of the recipe's group even when the recipe's household is locked and the admin is in another household, and false for an admin of another group.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

Frontend: `cd frontend && pnpm test:ci app/composables/recipes/__tests__/use-recipe-permissions.test.ts`.
643c4901.notes: Parametrized over the private and lock preferences (four cases); the request states the rule once.

3be8f3d8.text:
Fix: migration imports can reach other groups' data, and archives are unpacked without a size limit.

Two problems with POST /api/groups/migrations. First, the recipes in an archive are created as they come: a tool entry carrying another group's tool id links (and renames into the importer's group) that group's tool, and an ingredient's referencedRecipe pointing at another group's recipe slug links that recipe. Second, every migrator extracts the uploaded zip (and nested zips) with no bound, so a small archive can fill the disk.

Expected:
- Before a migrated recipe is created it goes through the recipe service's cleaning of an import (the same cleaning the zip import does): tools are resolved or created in the importer's group, so the imported recipe's tools all carry the importer's groupId and never the foreign id, and the other group's tool keeps its name and group; a referencedRecipe that is not the importer's is dropped (null). This holds for the Mealie alpha migrator and for the migrators that go through the scraper cleaner and pass tools through (Nextcloud and the others).
- A helper extract_zip(archive, dest, max_size=None) -> int in mealie.services.migrations.utils.migration_helpers: sums the declared sizes of the archive's members and raises ArchiveTooLargeError (a ValueError) before writing anything when the sum exceeds max_size (the destination is not created); otherwise extracts and returns the bytes written (max_size equal to the total is fine). The default is MAX_EXTRACTED_ARCHIVE_SIZE = 5 * 1024**3, a module constant tests may patch. Every zip-based migrator (Chowdown, Cook'n, Copy Me That, Mealie alpha, Nextcloud, Paprika, Plan to Eat, Recipe Keeper, Tandoor) extracts through it, and the ones that unpack nested archives pass what remains of the budget, so a zip of zips cannot multiply the limit.
- A too-large archive does not fail the request: the migration still answers 200 with its report; the report's status is "failure" and its only entry has the message "Archive is too large to import" (the exception text in the entry's exception field).
- Every supported migration (Nextcloud, Paprika, Chowdown, Copy Me That, Mealie alpha, Tandoor, Plan to Eat archive and CSV, My Recipe Box CSV, Recipe Keeper, Cook'n) keeps importing its archives exactly as before: recipes, categories, yields, notes, the rejection of a wrong file type for Plan to Eat and the skipping of bad Mealie alpha entries are unchanged.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/recipe_migration_tests tests/unit_tests/services_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
3be8f3d8.notes: The size test patches MAX_EXTRACTED_ARCHIVE_SIZE on the helpers module, so the constant name and module are stated. The selection also lists the pre-existing migration tests of the module as targets (they fail on the parent in the selector run, presumably through state the new cross-group test leaves behind there); the request states that existing migrations must keep working.

56d039c7.text:
Fix: a user-supplied query filter can escape the mandatory public filter.

The explore endpoints build their filter by string concatenation: "(<queryFilter>) AND (<public filter>)". A queryFilter such as name <> "zzz") OR (name <> "zzz" closes the group early and ORs the public condition away, so private recipes, cookbooks and households of a public group become visible; the same concatenation is used for the household member list, the mealplan date and plan-rule filters and the cookbook filter in the recipe repository. The parser only counts parentheses, so a group that closes before it opens passes.

Expected:
- QueryFilterBuilder.combine_filters(*filter_strings) (a classmethod): skips empty or None parts, validates each remaining part on its own by parsing it, and raises HTTPException 400 with the parser's message when a part is invalid; otherwise wraps each part in parentheses and joins them with " AND ". All the places above build their filter with it.
- The parser's parenthesis check tracks depth: a group that closes before it opens ('name <> "test name") OR (useAbbreviation=f') is rejected with ValueError "invalid query string: parenthesis are unbalanced", like a filter whose counts do not match.
- GET /api/explore/groups/{group_slug}/recipes?queryFilter=name <> "zzz") OR (name <> "zzz" on a public group with a public household answers 400 and never lists a private recipe. Valid filters keep working.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/public_explorer_tests tests/unit_tests/repository_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

97a66c19.text:
Feature: recipe counts, "delete unused" and merge for foods, tools and labels.

Tags and categories recently got a recipe count, a /empty list and a merge action. Foods, tools and multi-purpose labels need the same, and the existing /empty lists leak across groups.

Expected:
- GET /api/foods items carry recipeCount (distinct recipes whose ingredients use the food; 0 when none), also on a single GET /api/foods/{item_id}. GET /api/organizers/tools items carry recipeCount (recipes using the tool).
- GET /api/foods/empty: the caller's group's foods used by no recipe ingredient and by no shopping list item (a food still on a shopping list is not "unused", deleting it would break the list). GET /api/organizers/tools/empty: tools on no recipe. GET /api/groups/labels/empty: labels on no food and no shopping list item. All three answer a plain list (200). They, and the existing GET /api/organizers/tags/empty and /api/organizers/categories/empty, are limited to the caller's group: another group's unused item never appears (today the tag and category lists return it).
- POST /api/organizers/tools/merge, body {"fromId", "toId"}, behind the organize permission (403 without): 400 when the ids are equal, 404 when either is unknown in the group; otherwise recipes of the source are moved to the target (a recipe with both keeps one link), the source is deleted (GET of it 404), and the response is 200 with the target including recipeCount.
- POST /api/groups/labels/merge, same body and rules: foods labelled with the source get the target, shopping list items labelled with the source get the target, each shopping list's label-settings rows end with exactly one row for the target and none for the source (a list that already had a row for the target keeps that one), the source label is deleted (it no longer appears in GET /api/groups/labels), 200 with the target label. 404 and 400 as above.
- PUT /api/foods/merge: afterwards the target's recipeCount counts the recipes of both, recipes' ingredients point at the target, and the source answers 404.
- Frontend (not graded): the foods, tools and labels data pages show the counts and offer merge and delete-unused.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/category_tag_tool_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
97a66c19.notes: The hidden tests use new route constants (foods_empty, groups_labels_empty, groups_labels_merge, organizers_tools_empty, organizers_tools_merge) from tests/utils/api_routes; the harness exports the tests directory from the commit, so they are not stated.
